key_insight: By combining BB84 states with the classically accessible random-oracle model, the paper shows that efficient simulation-secure one-time memory remains possible even beyond NISQ-only assumptions.
engineering_relevance: This suggests a practical path to robust one-time quantum memory protocols for early fault-tolerant-era adversaries, using only modest quantum resources and quadratic communication.
method: Assume adversaries can only make classical queries to the random oracle (CAROM).
Construct one-time memory using only BB84 states plus classical data.
Prove simulation security with exponentially small advantage in the security parameter n.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports that with nℓ qubits and (n+2)λ classical bits, the simulation advantage is at most (n+3)(3/4)^n for adversaries limited to 2^{ℓ/2-1}-1 classical oracle queries.
watch_item: Security depends on the CAROM restriction and on the allowed number of classical random-oracle queries, so practical deployment would need confidence that quantum adversaries remain classically query-limited.
paper_title: Beyond NISQ Assumptions: One-time Memory in the Classically Accessible Random-Oracle Model
